newsitem.title: CANADA: AEC in talks to expand Syncrude pipeline.
newsitem.headline: AEC in talks to expand Syncrude pipeline.

text.p: Alberta Energy Co Ltd affiliate AEC Pipelines LP said on Tuesday it was in talks with Syncrude Canada Ltd to expand the pipeline that carries synthetic crude oil from the northern Alberta oil sands operation.

Syncrude, which is planning a major expansion of its oil sands mining, extraction and upgrading operation over the next few years, transports all of its 205,000 barrels per day of synthetic oil output on AEC's Alberta Oil Sands Pipe Line.
"As AOSPL is operating at capacity, discussions have been initiated with respect to options for the expansion of the AOSPL system by the partnership," AEC said.
"While these discussions are at an early stage, construction could commence in the first quarter of 1998, subject to the receipt of regulatory approvals," it said.
AEC Pipelines is a limited partnership which was floated by Alberta Energy last year. Its instalment receipts trade on the Toronto and Alberta stock exchanges.
Syncrude Canada Ltd, located north of Fort McMurray, Alberta, is the world's largest producer of synthetic crude oil.

Its partners include Imperial Oil Ltd, Petro-Canada, Gulf Canada Resources Ltd, Athabasca Oil Sands Investments Inc, Canadian Oil Sands Investments Inc, Alberta Energy Co Ltd, Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, Mitsubishi Oil Co Ltd unit Mocal Energy Ltd and Murphy Oil Corp.
AEC Pipelines has already applied with partner Husky Oil Ltd to build its Lakeland Pipeline, which would carry heavy oil to Hardisty, Alberta from Fort McMurray, Alberta.
The proposal is one of several aimed at boosting transport capacity from fast growing volumes of Canadian heavy oil from the region.

AEC Pipelines also said on Tuesday that net income for its inital quarter of operations as a public entity, ended June 30, was C$14.4 million or C13 cents per unit and distributable income was C$23.5 million or C22 cents per unit.
